cards.front: What does a frame round trip establish?
cards.back: Algebraic consistency, not measured physical calibration accuracy.

cards.front: How does small orientation error move a point?
cards.back: Its tangential displacement is approximately radius times angular error in radians.
Variance combination requires stated covariance assumptions; magnitude sums can represent conservative bounds.

cards.front: What do the Jacobian columns describe?
cards.back: Instantaneous endpoint velocity per unit rate of each joint at the current pose.
Exact weak-direction tracking in exchange for reduced inverse-rate amplification.

cards.front: How is force mapped to joint torque?
cards.back: JᵀF, with consistent frame and sign convention, preserves virtual power.

cards.front: Does singular inverse velocity imply divergent JᵀF?
cards.back: No; prescribed velocity and prescribed force are different calculations.
Substitute them into forward geometry, then check joint intervals and collision constraints.

cards.front: Are two elbow branches continuous redundancy?
cards.back: No; a nonsingular two-joint position arm has no extra continuous degree of freedom.
No; elbows, link bodies and swept geometry need their own checks.

cards.front: Do sampled clearances prove continuous clearance?
cards.back: Only with additional valid motion bounds or a continuous geometric argument.
The quadratic kinetic-energy form K=½q̇ᵀMq̇ for the declared mechanics.
The potential-energy gradient included with positive sign in the actuator balance.

cards.front: Can M stay positive definite at endpoint rank loss?
cards.back: Yes; other moving masses can still constrain every joint-velocity direction.

cards.front: What checks a no-loss dynamic equation?
cards.back: Actuator power equals the derivative of kinetic plus potential energy under the declared forces.

cards.front: Which operating point determines torque availability?
cards.back: Voltage, current cap and speed together under the stated motoring model.
An ideal rigid reduction reflects J_m as N²J_m at the output.

cards.front: What limits a motor-side encoder claim?
cards.back: Its count spacing does not observe all output backlash, compliance or frame error.

cards.front: What does ideal PD analysis omit?
cards.back: Sampling, delay, saturation and omitted mechanics can change the response and stability.
A path specifies geometry; time scaling specifies its execution timing.

cards.front: What is the cubic peak speed?
cards.back: For a scalar move it is 1.5|Δq|/T, with generally nonzero endpoint acceleration.

cards.front: What is the conditional stop allowance?
cards.back: Latency travel plus braking travel plus a separately declared position allowance.

cards.front: Can slower timing remove a collision?
cards.back: No; slowing the same path changes dynamics but leaves its geometry.
A stated command-minus-measurement convention with synchronized time, units and sensor identity.

cards.front: Does an excessive sensor jump identify one fault?
cards.back: No; it flags a discrepancy relative to a justified bound and error model.
Independent output sensing, reversal/load dependence and a declared mechanical model.

cards.front: How is the stall case bounded?
cards.back: Check inverse rates, delivered actuation, dynamics and sensing separately; a checklist is not hardware validation.
Keep task direction and posture together when summarizing signed velocity components.
Scale all inverse rates together to preserve the desired direction under the frozen Jacobian while reducing speed.
A finite radial force can have zero joint moment at rank loss even though instantaneous radial motion is unavailable.
Toy limiter reports constrain one mathematical explanation without identifying a physical stall or validating a protective function.
